stem.text: Sand is delivered to a building site at a rate of P(t) tons per hour, where P is differentiable and t is measured in hours. Measured values are P(1) = 6, P(2) = 9, P(5) = 11, P(7) = 4. Find the approximation to \( \int_{1}^{7} P(t)\,dt \), the number of tons of sand delivered from t = 1 to t = 7, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 1 \cdot \frac{6 + 9}{2} = \frac{15}{2} \); \( 3 \cdot \frac{9 + 11}{2} = 30 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{11 + 4}{2} = 15 \).

distractor_derivations.A: trapezoidal sum with the common width (b - a)/3 used for every subinterval
distractor_derivations.B: left Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.D: trapezoid area taken as width times the sum of the two endpoint values, with no division by 2
